newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Koor in negotiations to sell Shemen unit.
newsitem.headline: Koor in negotiations to sell Shemen unit.

text.p: Israel's Koor Industries is in talks to sell its 71.5 percent stake in Shemen Industries Ltd to an Israeli investment fund and a U.S. investor, a source close to the talks said on Monday.
The prospective buyers are the Challenge Fund, an Israeli venture capital fund, and an unidentified U.S. investor. The daily newspaper Maariv said the two were seeking to recruit a third partner.

The source said the sale valued Shemen, a maker of edible oils and personal care products, at $40 million. But, he added, the sale would "not necessarily" include Shemen's 50-percent-controlled Henkel Soad personal care products unit.
The remainder of Henkel Soad is controlled by Germany's Henkel KGaA.
A Koor spokesman declined to comment on the reports. Officials from the Challenge Fund were unavailable for comment.

The sale would be in line with Koor's strategy of exiting from the food industry, which is not among the sectors the company has chosen to focus on. In February Koor sold its remaining 24.5 percent stake in Israel Edible Products (Tami) and is reportedly looking for buyers for its smaller holdings.

Shemen's market capitalisation is only $28.3 million and its shareholders' equity stands at about $20 million, but the company holds considerable real estate in Haifa and the Tel Aviv suburb of Petah Tikva.
